ai.description: *Indirana duboisi* is a small frog (25–30 mm) with a brown dorsum and dark lateral bands. It features a pointed snout, a distinct white spot on the tympanum, and granular skin on the flanks.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Indirana duboisi* is best identified by the presence of a distinct, continuous white or cream-colored band running along the upper lip, which is absent in similar species.
ai.habitat: *Indirana duboisi* inhabits the leaf litter and rocky stream banks of moist evergreen forests in the Western Ghats, typically at elevations between 800 and 1,200 meters.
ai.behavior: Dubois's Leaping Frog is primarily nocturnal, spending its active hours foraging for small invertebrates along the rocky, moss-covered banks of fast-flowing forest streams.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Indirana duboisi* breeds during the monsoon, laying clutches of 100–300 eggs on moist rocks or vegetation near streams, where larvae develop in semi-aquatic environments.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Indirana duboisi* is endemic to the Western Ghats of India, primarily inhabiting high-elevation evergreen forests in the states of Kerala and Tamil Nadu.
ai.callDescription: The advertisement call of *Indirana duboisi* consists of a series of short, high-pitched, metallic chirps emitted from rocky, wet habitats near fast-flowing forest streams.
